title: The γ ≤ 1/2 campaign
convention: Weights are the estimated size of each work package (thousands of new Lean lines; non-Lean steps get an equivalent weight). A finished package counts fully once it passes its checks and an independent re-run of its audit. A running package counts by the orchestrator's estimate at its last checkpoint (what is proved against what remains); before its first checkpoint it counts by the Lean it has compiled, capped at 75 %. Line counts alone overstate progress, because several packages first port large amounts of the existing proof.
next: The γ ≤ 1/2 final count is proved. Remaining: the stage-1 vine case (last port modules), the γ ≤ 1/2 flower estimate (marked stage 1 and marked count), then landing, sealing and two-key audits.
risks: new mathematics may need local repairs once formalized
integration: about a dozen packages must meet at exact interfaces
